lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Central Exchange. Connecting calls between universes since nineteen forty six.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Number, please.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: You've reached the Switchboard, on one hundred and thirty one point one.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Please hold. Please keep holding. You're doing very well.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: The Switchboard. Every line in the multiverse comes through this room. The room is mostly cords.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: This is the Exchange. I connect. I don't listen.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I hear, which is different. And I repeat nothing.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: The Switchboard. If you can hear this, you dialled correctly. Very few people dial correctly.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: It's gone eleven, and every light on the board is lit. Everybody rings home after dark.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: This is the Night Exchange. Hold the line.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Good morning. The lines are clear, the rates are low, and the past is cheaper before nine.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Early Trunk Calls, from the Exchange.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Advice, then the news, then the traffic. You rang in the right order.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Hardly anyone does. Most people ring the news first, and then they're too worried to ring anyone else.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Welcome to the Exchange. Mind the cords.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Well. A new light on the board. You found us the old way, one station after another, like a number you half remembered.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I've given you a lamp. It's a small one. It's yours. Try to keep it lit.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Quiet on the board tonight. Three lights. One of them has been lit since nineteen fifty eight.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I've never put it through. They've never asked me to. Some calls just like to wait.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: People ask whether I listen in. I don't. But you can't sit at a switchboard for eighty years without learning what a pause means.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Most calls are pauses. The words are just the bits around them.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: A note on rates. Calls to neighbouring universes are charged at the local rate. Distant universes, at the long distance rate.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Calls to the universe where you said the right thing at the time are not currently available. I'm sorry. Everyone asks.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Somebody once asked me who I ring, when I want to talk to someone.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I said, nobody. I'm the one in the middle. Then I put them through, and went back to my tea.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: The cords on this board, laid end to end, would reach every place anybody has ever missed.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I measured once. It took a while. I had a quiet decade.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: There's a relay ship that rings the exchange now and then. The Nightjar. Lovely manners. Never says much.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: She asks for the same number every time. Then she says, never mind. Not yet. And hangs up.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Midnight is the busy hour. Everyone who couldn't say it in the day rings to say it now.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I've two hands and nine hundred cords. Please be patient. Your call is important. They all are. That's the trouble.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: First light, and the long lines are humming. A call to nineteen sixty three has just gone through, clear as a bell.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Mornings are good for the past. It's still half asleep. It doesn't argue.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Number, please.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Thank you. Connecting you now. Hold the line.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Trunk call, coming through. One moment.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: You're through. Go ahead, caller.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Central. I'm putting you through to a universe I've never had a call from.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: This should be interesting. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Long distance. Very long distance.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Please speak clearly, and allow for the delay. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: You're connected. Mind the crackle.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: That's just time, getting in the way.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Stayed
lines.text: Hello? Is that me? The one who took the lighthouse job?

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Went
lines.text: It's me. I took the lighthouse.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Stayed
lines.text: Is it nice?

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Went
lines.text: It's very quiet.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Stayed
lines.text: Good. I hoped it would be quiet.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Went
lines.text: How's the flat?

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Stayed
lines.text: Loud. I like it.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Went
lines.text: Good. I hoped you would.

lines.speaker: A Caller with a Library Book
lines.text: Hello, is that the library on Carrow Street? The one that wasn't knocked down?

lines.speaker: A Librarian
lines.text: Speaking.

lines.speaker: A Caller with a Library Book
lines.text: I've got one of your books. I'm afraid it's forty years overdue.

lines.speaker: A Librarian
lines.text: Forty? It's only been a week, here.

lines.speaker: A Caller with a Library Book
lines.text: Oh. Then I'm only a week late.

lines.speaker: A Librarian
lines.text: Just the week. We'll say no more about it. Did you like it?

lines.speaker: A Caller with a Library Book
lines.text: I read it every year.

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: Biscuit? Biscuit, is that you?

lines.speaker: Biscuit, a Dog
lines.text: Hello! Hello! Is it you? It's you!

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: Are you being a good boy?

lines.speaker: Biscuit, a Dog
lines.text: I'm being the best boy. I've been the best boy all day. Nobody here can tell, though.

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: I can tell. I'll ring again on Sunday.

lines.speaker: Biscuit, a Dog
lines.text: What's Sunday?

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: Soon.

lines.speaker: Biscuit, a Dog
lines.text: I love soon!

lines.speaker: A Caller, Aged Ninety
lines.text: Hello. Is that the dance hall? Nineteen fifty two? The night of the competition?

lines.speaker: A Girl at the Dance Hall
lines.text: It is. Who's this?

lines.speaker: A Caller, Aged Ninety
lines.text: Never mind who. Did we win?

lines.speaker: A Girl at the Dance Hall
lines.text: We won.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Aged Ninety
lines.text: Was I any good?

lines.speaker: A Girl at the Dance Hall
lines.text: You were terrible. You trod on him twice. We won anyway.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Aged Ninety
lines.text: That's how I remember it.

lines.speaker: A Wrong Number
lines.text: Sorry. I think I've got the wrong universe.

lines.speaker: Another Wrong Number
lines.text: So have I.

lines.speaker: A Wrong Number
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Another Wrong Number
lines.text: Shall we just stay on a minute?

lines.speaker: A Wrong Number
lines.text: Yes. If that's all right.

lines.speaker: Another Wrong Number
lines.text: It's all right.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I'll leave this one connected.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Very Late
lines.text: Operator, could you put me through to anyone who's awake?

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Anyone at all?

lines.speaker: A Caller, Very Late
lines.text: Anyone at all.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Connecting you to anyone.

lines.speaker: Anyone
lines.text: Hello?

lines.speaker: A Caller, Very Late
lines.text: Hello. I'm awake.

lines.speaker: Anyone
lines.text: So am I.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Very Late
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Anyone
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: A Concerned Neighbour
lines.text: Hello, is that the universe next door? I think you've left your iron on.

lines.speaker: The Universe Next Door
lines.text: We don't have irons.

lines.speaker: A Concerned Neighbour
lines.text: Then what's that smell?

lines.speaker: The Universe Next Door
lines.text: That's Tuesday. It always smells like that.

lines.speaker: A Concerned Neighbour
lines.text: Oh. Sorry to bother you.

lines.speaker: The Universe Next Door
lines.text: Not at all. Thank you for checking. Nobody ever checks.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Moved Away
lines.text: Hello, Mum? It's me. From the one where I moved away.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: Hello, love. You sound far.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Moved Away
lines.text: I am. Tell me about the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: The kitchen? It's the same. The clock's still slow. The radio's on. Your coat's on the hook.

lines.speaker: A Caller, Who Moved Away
lines.text: Tell me about the kitchen again.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: The clock's still slow, love.

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: Hello. Is that the dream I had on Tuesday?

lines.speaker: A Dream, Tuesday's
lines.text: Speaking.

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: I just wanted to say sorry. About the bit with the stairs.

lines.speaker: A Dream, Tuesday's
lines.text: Which bit?

lines.speaker: A Caller
lines.text: You know which bit.

lines.speaker: A Dream, Tuesday's
lines.text: Oh. That bit. Nobody minded. The stairs thought it was funny.

lines.speaker: A Caller in a Phone Box
lines.text: And tell her I'll be home—

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Please insert another coin, or a small regret. Either is accepted.

lines.speaker: A Caller in a Phone Box
lines.text: Here.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Thank you. That's a large regret. You have six minutes.

lines.speaker: A Caller in a Phone Box
lines.text: Tell her I'm sorry about the shed.

lines.speaker: Somebody at Home
lines.text: She says she knows. She says, come home.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Your party has hung up.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Your party has hung up. They said goodbye first. I thought you'd want to know.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: That line has cleared. I didn't hear a word.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Next caller, please.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: The other universe has gone quiet. Please replace the receiver. Gently. It remembers.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Call ended. The charges have been reversed, and then reversed again, so nobody owes anybody.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: That's how I like it.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Every light on the board has just lit up. Everybody ringing about a moon.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: None of them has it. So I've connected them all to each other. They're comparing skies. It seems to help.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: The whole exchange smells of toast. I've sat at this board since nineteen forty six, and nobody has ever offered me any.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I'm putting that on the record. And taking it off again. Discretion.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Every line on the board is humming the same half a tune. Callers keep asking me how it ends.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I could tell them. I've heard it finished, on a call in nineteen fifty one. But I repeat nothing.

clips.title: You Don't Knock on an Exchange

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Three knocks on the exchange door. In eighty years, nobody has knocked. You don't knock on a switchboard. You ring it.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I've kept the door shut, and left a line open. In case they'd rather call.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: Every lamp on the board has gone the new colour. I can't tell which light is which.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: So I'm putting everyone through to everyone. Strangers, talking about the sky. Best night we've had in years.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: There is a pigeon standing on the switchboard. It has just connected Gristwick to the bottom of the sea.

lines.speaker: The Operator
lines.text: I don't usually allow visitors at the board. It seems to have a pass.
